package_info.why_malicious: The package itself is not inherently malicious, but running Nexus Repository Manager 2.x on Java 7 exposes users to unpatched vulnerabilities due to unsupported dependencies. As future security fixes may require Java 8, users persisting with Java 7 will be unable to apply critical patches, leaving the application and its data at risk of exploitation.

attack_chain.action: A vulnerability is disclosed in an open source dependency used by Nexus Repository Manager 2.x.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential exploitation if the vulnerability is not patched.

attack_chain.action: A fix for the vulnerability is released, but it requires upgrading to Java 8 due to dependency requirements.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users on Java 7 cannot apply the fix.

attack_chain.action: Users who have not upgraded to Java 8 remain exposed to the publicized, exploitable vulnerability.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential compromise of the repository manager and its data.

behavioral_signatures: Deployment of Nexus Repository Manager 2.x on Java 7 runtime environments
Detection of outdated or unsupported Java runtime versions in production systems
Failure to apply recent security patches due to Java version incompatibility
file_indicators: Presence of Java 7 runtime (java version '1.7.*') on systems running Nexus Repository Manager 2.x
Nexus Repository Manager 2.x installation directories (e.g., /opt/sonatype/nexus or similar paths)
network_indicators: No direct network indicators; risk arises from exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities in the application or its dependencies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for instances of Nexus Repository Manager 2.x running on Java 7 by checking the Java runtime version used by the application process. Flag and alert on any deployments where the Java version is 1.7.x and the application cannot be updated to the latest security patch due to Java version constraints. Proactively notify administrators to upgrade to Java 8 or later to ensure the ability to apply future security fixes and maintain a secure environment.
